chunks: Saʿd ibn ʿAbd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Musa ibn al-Qasim and Abu Qatadah, from ʿAli ibn Jaʿfar, from his brother Musa ibn Jaʿfar عليهما السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who performed wudu (ablution) but forgot to wash his left [hand]. He said: “He should wash only his left [hand], and he does not repeat the wudu (ablution) of anything other than it.”

Then he said: This report indicates the opposite of what you have mentioned regarding the obligation of sequence, because if it were obligatory, he would not have allowed repeating the washing of the left [hand] alone, since in that case it would become the last of the limbs in the taharah (ritual purification).

We said: The meaning of this report is that he does not repeat the wudu (ablution) of anything other than it from what came before it, not what came after it, such as washing the face and the right hand. As for what came after it, it is obligatory to repeat its wiping, and that which indicates this is as follows.

key_terms.التَّرْتِيبِ: the required sequence/order between the acts of wudu
key_terms.غَسْلَ: washing of a limb in ritual purification
key_terms.مَسْحِهَا: wiping it, referring to the limbs that are wiped in wudu
key_terms.وُضُوءَ: wudu (ablution), the ritual act of purification
key_terms.يَسَارِهِ: his left hand/side, referring here to the left hand in wudu

ai.seo_question: If someone forgets to wash the left hand in wudu (ablution), must the entire wudu be repeated?
ai.summary: This text discusses a legal ruling concerning sequence in wudu (ablution), specifically when washing the left hand was forgotten. It explains that the report does not negate the obligation of order; rather, only what preceded the omitted limb is not repeated, while what followed it must be redone.
